'''Lyudmyla Oleksandrivna Nazarova''' ({{langx|uk|Людмила Олександрівна Назарова}}, published as L. A. Nazarova and also spelled Liudmila, Ludmila, or Lyudmila; born 14 May 1938 in [[Vologda]], [[RSFSR]]<ref name="esu">{{cite book |trans-chapter=Nazarova Lyudmyla Oleksandrivna | chapter=Назарова Людмила Олександрівна |url=https://esu.com.ua/search_articles.php?id=71685 |title=Encyclopedia of Modern Ukraine | date=12 December 2020 | volume=22 | publisher=Інститут енциклопедичних досліджень НАН України | isbn=978-966-02-2074-4 }}</ref>) is a [[Ukraine|Ukrainian]] mathematician specializing in [[linear algebra]] and [[representation theory]].

==Research==
With her husband, [[Andrei Vladimirovich Roiter]], Nazarova founded the theory of representations of and differentiation of [[partially ordered set]]s,{{r|yakovlev|hammocks}}{{ran|A}} and solved the second Brauer–Thrall conjecture, [[mathematical proof|proving]] what became known as the Nazarova–Roiter theorem.{{r|ringel|fisch|bretod}}{{ran|B}}
Her research has also included pioneering work on representations of [[quiver (mathematics)|quiver]]s,{{ran|C}} and on the [[wild problem]] in [[matrix (mathematics)|matrix]] classification.{{ran|D}}

==Education and career==
Lyudmila Nazarova was born in a family of mathematician Olxander Nazarov.{{r|esu}}
Nazarova began her studies at [[Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv]], where she met Roiter. Together they transferred to [[Leningrad State University]],{{r|roiter}} where Nazarova completed her doctorate as a student of [[Dmitry Faddeev]].{{r|mg}} They returned to Kiev,{{r|roiter}} and Nazarova became a researcher in the Institute of Mathematics of the Academy of Sciences of Ukraine, now the [[National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine]]. She has since retired.{{r|imath}}
